A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPMF research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original Gaussian simulations, neural SB experiments, image translations, and quantitative evaluations. Explicitly borrowed benchmark rows are distinguished from the work's own results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional Gaussian diagnostics and CelebA experiments with SDEdit-based initializations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The IPMF projection sequence and ASBM/DSBM fitting algorithms remain unchanged. V2 adds a concrete initialization component: constructing couplings through SDEdit using either a CelebA-trained DDPM or pretrained Stable Diffusion 1.5 (Appendix C.3). This extends initialization without redesigning the fitting procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian transport, Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll translation, the same SB mixtures benchmark, colored-MNIST 3-to-2 translation, and CelebA male-to-female translation. SDEdit initializations retain the CelebA population and task; the changed Gaussian dimensionality is a setting revision within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same comparison methods, including SF2M-Sink, the best-benchmark row, and the ASBM/DSBM initialization variants. The added SDEdit pipelines construct initial couplings within IPMF; they are not evaluated as standalone competing SB solvers.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the Gaussian experiment from D=16 to D=128 at epsilon=0.3. Table 3 changes the stated initial DSBM training budget for CelebA Ind(p0,p0) from 20,000 to 100,000 gradient updates. V2 also introduces protocols for the SDEdit initialization experiments; these disclosures do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 extends initialization analysis to learned image-translation couplings, testing their effects on target fit and input preservation using both solvers (Figures 5, 6, and 8). Figure 2 also adds separate optimality-matrix, mean, and covariance diagnostics beyond v1's aggregate KL curves, substantially expanding the evidence about how convergence proceeds.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates and individual curves. The benchmark's Monte Carlo estimation descriptions, including 1,000 conditional samples and 10,000 target-distribution samples, are retained.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the Gaussian curves with results for D=128 and adds parameter-convergence outcomes. CelebA gains SDEdit results and revisions to existing curves: terminal DSBM-IMF MSE changes from approximately 0.42 to 0.18 (v1 Figure 7b; v2 Figure 8b), without explaining that revision. These are reported-result changes, not established same-setting performance gains. All numerical entries in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's scalar optimality coefficient and Gaussian-plan lemma become an optimality matrix and multidimensional Theorem 3.1. Theorem 3.2 extends exponential convergence to D>1 for discrete IMF with N=1 and sufficiently large epsilon. Appendix B adds matrix marginal bounds, Lipschitz analysis, and convergence proofs, while retaining the scalar analysis.

C1.justification: V1's introduction explicitly limits its proved convergence contribution to one-dimensional Gaussians. V2 broadens this central contribution to Gaussian convergence under several settings, including the restricted multidimensional case. The identification of bidirectional IMF with IPMF and the conjecture of more general convergence remain.

C2.justification: V1 describes approximately equal CelebA target fit and groups MSE behavior mainly by solver. V2 interprets results through initialization-dependent target-fit and input-preservation tradeoffs, and explains why SDEdit couplings could begin closer to both desired marginals and an SB solution. General convergence remains an acknowledged limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix C.9 adds DDPM training specifications, SDEdit noising/denoising settings, the Stable Diffusion model identifier and prompt, guidance settings, resizing instructions, and implementation sources. Section 4.1 newly specifies three uniformly spaced intermediate times; v1 does not establish a different grid. Most existing implementation information moves from Appendix D to C.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting SDEdit, DDPM, latent diffusion, and matrix analysis, among others. It removes Ibe (2013) and Janati et al. (2020), including the latter's role in qualifying the earlier scalar Gaussian result. The central positioning as a unification of IPF and IMF is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Contributions are reorganized, Gaussian proofs are restructured, experimental appendices C and D are consolidated, and broader impact moves into the main text. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 converts the main text and references to two columns, adds the IPF/IMF/IPMF schematic, expands Gaussian diagnostics and CelebA displays, and restructures Table 3. The Swiss-roll figure moves to Appendix C with identical images, while colored-MNIST visuals are retained and rearranged. V2 also introduces the placeholder running header 'Title Suppressed Due to Excessive Size'.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is the extension from scalar-only convergence theory to a multidimensional analysis with explicit restrictions and supporting proofs (Section 3.2 and Appendix B), addressing a substantial part of v1's theoretical limitation. SDEdit experiments additionally connect initialization flexibility to practical image-preservation behavior. General convergence remains open, and unexplained revisions to existing CelebA curves limit empirical comparisons, but the stronger theoretical support and broader mechanism analysis provide a substantial net improvement.
